why: Euclid on strings: a common divisor exists only if str1 + str2 == str2 + str1, and then the longest one has length gcd(len1, len2), so the answer is the prefix of that length.
hints: If t divides both strings, what can you say about str1 + str2 versus str2 + str1?
They are equal (both are copies of t). Conversely, if they are equal, a common divisor exists.
If str1 + str2 != str2 + str1 return ''. Otherwise return str1[:gcd(len(str1), len(str2))]. O(len1 + len2).
pitfalls: When no divisor exists, return the empty string.
The longest divisor's length is the gcd of the lengths, not the minimum length.
